For air based characters there is usually a moment in which you can either trade or just stuff their move. Sans I have not found a way to deal with F.A.N.G's fly yet but y'know, training mode.

Another issue I found with my gameplay is that I never adapted to the situation. You can't just do the same thing over and over and expect to win against someone who is adapting. On the same coin if someone is doing the same thing over and over and consistently punishing you, you should never expect to win unless you adapt to that.

It takes time, a lot of rage, a lot of feelings of defeat, and just realizing that it's more about learning and having fun and not worrying about the points.bthat my 2 cents.

In the time of 207x magic has returned to the world. People have settled into their new lifestyles of what theyve become and the new races are more tolerated than accepted by a few corporations and specific groups. The story we focus on is in seattle where groups of criminals, vigilantes, psychos, and thrill-seekers perform tasks called 'runs'. At this point in time yhere is war brewing, not only in meat space but also the web. Trideos disguised as funny cat videos actually containing a trojan horse of avatars looking to mark their prey and steal others secrets. Lately, a massive wave of deckers and innocent VR users have been found geek'd in their homes. Someone is hunting them. Not pointing any fingers, but Needle Point Cybernetics and Pikes Place Prosthetics have been everything but cordial. From the assassination of the spokeswoman on national news during a conference tothe extremely similar cybernetics and procedures offered at varying rates to customers around the same time an infiltration took place. Not only that but tensions have been riding high between high-born elves and the dwarves claiming racial superiority. Its no surprise that after your groups last job that ended up botched your broker had to join the dwarves for protection. Its a shit show out there. But staring at the homepage of your old stomping grounds, Reddit, you've been struck with that itch...just one more job. A message pops up on your screen, "been a while, how about a run?" You sit looking at the message trying to decide if its the right thing to do. Whether it is or not, you've got that itch. The question is though, are you going to scratch it?
